about: Light through gas (ND2): one mechanism for every gas and every body, with no kind of body named. A gas's features (measured bands, pressure-widened lines, colliding pairs) are rows on the master data sheet; these blocks are the physics that turns them into the light that comes out.

references: Rybicki, G. B. and Lightman, A. P. 1979, Radiative Processes in Astrophysics, Wiley, section 10.6 (the classical oscillator: a line's integrated cross-section is πe²f/(m_e c) in Gaussian units, e²f/(4ε₀m_e c) in SI) and section 1.6 (stimulated emission). doi:10.1002/9783527618170
atoms.shown: S = e² f / (4 ε₀ m_e c) · e^(−E_l / kT) · (1 − e^(−hc / λ₀kT))

equation.name: How strongly one atom absorbs at a line, in all
equation.formula:
pop = exp(-El / (k * T))
stim = -expm1(-h * c / (lambda0 * k * T))
S = e * e / (4 * eps0 * me * c) * f * pop * stim

f.name: oscillator strength of the line (how many electrons' worth it absorbs)

El.name: energy of the level the line absorbs from, above the ground state

S.name: cross-section of one atom summed over the whole line (per hertz of width)

source.text: Rybicki, G. B. and Lightman, A. P. 1979, Radiative Processes in Astrophysics

explain.curious: Each kind of atom swallows light at its own sharp colours. How much it swallows in all is fixed by the atom; the gas's heat decides how many atoms are ready to.
explain.science: Integrated line cross-section of a classical oscillator of strength f, times the Boltzmann share of absorbers in the lower level (relative to the ground level; the partition function is a stand-in) and the correction for stimulated emission.

references: Gray, D. F. 2005, The Observation and Analysis of Stellar Photospheres, 3rd ed., Cambridge University Press, chapter 11 (thermal Doppler width, radiation damping, van der Waals widening growing with perturber density and as T^0.3). doi:10.1017/CBO9780511614576

equation.name: How wide a line is spread by heat and by crowding
equation.formula:
sd = sqrt(k * T / m) / lambda0
gl = (G0 + Cw * n * (T / T0) ^ x) / (4 * pi)

m.name: mass of one absorbing atom or molecule

G0.name: natural damping rate of the line (from the levels' lifetimes)

Cw.name: damping added per perturbing particle per cubic metre, at the reference temperature

n.name: number of perturbing particles per cubic metre

x.name: how the widening per particle grows with temperature (0.3 for van der Waals)

T0.name: temperature the widening per particle was measured at

sd.name: spread of the line in frequency from the atoms' thermal motion (one standard deviation)

gl.name: half width of the line's damping wings in frequency

source.text: Gray, D. F. 2005, The Observation and Analysis of Stellar Photospheres, 3rd ed.

explain.curious: A line is never perfectly sharp. Hot atoms rush to and fro and smear it; in a dense gas, neighbours jostle each atom mid-swallow and spread its wings wide. That crowding is what makes a cool, dense white dwarf's sodium line hundreds of nanometres broad.
explain.science: Thermal Doppler standard deviation in frequency, and the Lorentzian half width (HWHM) of radiation damping plus collisional widening linear in perturber density, scaled as a power of temperature.

equation.name: Width of a line spread by heat and crowding together
equation.formula:
fg = 2 * sqrt(2 * ln(2)) * sd
fl = 2 * gl
F = (fg ^ 5 + a1 * fg ^ 4 * fl + a2 * fg ^ 3 * fl ^ 2 + a3 * fg ^ 2 * fl ^ 3 + a4 * fg * fl ^ 4 + fl ^ 5) ^ (1/5)
r = fl / F
eta = e1 * r - e2 * r * r + e3 * r * r * r

sd.name: spread from thermal motion (one standard deviation)

gl.name: half width of the damping wings

F.name: full width at half depth of the combined line shape

eta.name: share of the line shape that is damping wings rather than the thermal core

source.text: Thompson, P., Cox, D. E. and Hastings, J. B. 1987, J. Appl. Cryst. 20, 79

explain.curious: Heat gives a line a rounded core and crowding gives it long wings. This finds the width of the two together and how much of the shape is wing.
explain.science: The pseudo-Voigt approximation: a weighted sum of a Gaussian and a Lorentzian of one common FWHM, with the TCH fits for that FWHM and the Lorentzian share; within about 1 % of the Voigt profile.

checks.says: damping share must lie between 0 and 1, got {}

references: Thompson, P., Cox, D. E. and Hastings, J. B. 1987, Rietveld refinement of Debye-Scherrer synchrotron X-ray data from Al2O3, J. Appl. Cryst. 20, 79: the pseudo-Voigt width and mixing fits (eqs. 3 and 4), good to about 1 % of the true Voigt. doi:10.1107/S0021889887087090
atoms.shown: φ(Δν) = η L(Δν) + (1 − η) G(Δν), both of full width f

equation.name: How much of a line falls at each colour near it
equation.formula:
hw = F / 2
L = hw / (pi * (dnu * dnu + hw * hw))
G = sqrt(4 * ln(2) / pi) / F * exp(-4 * ln(2) * dnu * dnu / (F * F))
phi = eta * L + (1 - eta) * G

dnu.name: distance in frequency from the line's centre

F.name: full width at half depth of the line shape

eta.name: share of the shape that is damping wings

phi.name: share of the line's strength per hertz at this distance from its centre

source.text: Thompson, P., Cox, D. E. and Hastings, J. B. 1987, J. Appl. Cryst. 20, 79

explain.curious: A line is strongest at its centre and fades away on both sides; in a dense gas its wings reach far into neighbouring colours.
explain.science: Pseudo-Voigt profile normalised to one over frequency: η times a Lorentzian plus (1 − η) times a Gaussian, both of FWHM f.

explain.curious: Molecules such as methane absorb in broad bands made of countless lines. Those are measured in the laboratory and looked up, then adjusted for how warm the gas is.
explain.science: A tabulated band cross-section at its measured temperature, scaled by a power of temperature (zero when the source gives no dependence).

explain.curious: Some molecules, such as hydrogen, cannot absorb on their own but can while two of them collide. Squeeze the gas and collisions grow with the square of its density, so dense hydrogen turns dark in the infrared.
explain.science: Collision-induced absorption: optical depth is the binary coefficient times the partner's number density times the absorber's column.

references: Gray, D. F., The Observation and Analysis of Stellar Photospheres, 3rd edn, Cambridge University Press, chapter 11 (van der Waals broadening: Unsöld's ΔC6 from the hydrogen-like sizes of the two levels, and the width γ6 = 17 v^(3/5) C6^(2/5) N). doi:10.1017/CBO9781316036570

Unsöld, A. 1955, Physik der Sternatmosphären, 2nd edn, Springer: the interaction C6 = e² α ⟨Δr²⟩ / h with ⟨r²⟩ ≈ (5/2) n*⁴ a0² and n*² = Ry / (I − E). https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-642-87452-5

Barklem, P. S., Piskunov, N. and O'Mara, B. J. 2000, A list of data for the broadening of metallic lines by neutral hydrogen collisions, Astron. Astrophys. Suppl. 142, 467: Unsöld's widths are often about two times too small; measured or computed widths take precedence. doi:10.1051/aas:2000167

equation.name: How much a crowd of neighbours widens a line (van der Waals)
equation.formula:
Ry = h * c * Rinf
Eu = El + h * c / lambda0
du = I - Eu
dl = I - El
C6 = if du <= 0 or dl <= 0 then 0 else e * e / (4 * pi * eps0) * ap * a0 * a0 * (5/2) * Ry * Ry / h * (1 / (du * du) - 1 / (dl * dl))
v = sqrt(8 * k * T / pi * (1 / ma + 1 / mp))
c6 = max(C6, 0)
Cw = lindholm * (v * v * v * c6 * c6) ^ (1/5)

I.name: energy to tear the outer electron off the absorbing atom

El.name: energy of the level the line absorbs from, above the ground state

ma.name: mass of one absorbing atom or molecule

ap.name: how easily the neighbour's charge is pulled out of shape (polarisability volume)

lindholm.name: number in the van der Waals width

Cw.name: damping added per perturbing particle per cubic metre, at the reference temperature

C6.name: strength of the pull between the atom and a neighbour, falling as the sixth power of distance

source.text: Gray, D. F., The Observation and Analysis of Stellar Photospheres, 3rd edn

explain.curious: In a dense gas every atom is jostled by its neighbours, and each brush shifts its colour a little. The more crowded and the hotter the gas, the wider the line, which is why sodium paints broad dark wings across the light of dense, cool atmospheres.
explain.science: Unsöld's hydrogen-like estimate of the C6 interaction from the two levels' effective quantum numbers and the perturber's polarisability, and the Lindholm impact width γ6 = 17 v^(3/5) C6^(2/5) N at the mean relative speed.
